Measuring salt

A level teaspoon of fine table salt weighs about 6 g. This page uses table salt because it's what most recipes mean when they just say salt.

Kosher salt is where conversions go wrong. Its crystals are bigger and hollower, so a teaspoon holds much less salt by weight: about 2.8 g for Diamond Crystal and about 4.8 g for Morton kosher salt. Using table salt in a recipe written for Diamond Crystal can make it twice as salty. When a recipe names a brand of kosher salt, weighing is the safest way to substitute.

Source: Morton table salt label (¼ teaspoon = 1.5 g); King Arthur Baking ingredient weight chart.

Questions

How many grams is 1 tablespoon of salt?

1 tablespoon (3 teaspoons) of salt weighs about 18 g. A level teaspoon is about 6 g.

How many teaspoons is 10 grams of salt?

10 g of salt is 1⅔ tsp, measured with level spoons.

How many grams is a teaspoon of kosher salt?

It depends on the brand. Diamond Crystal kosher salt is about 2.8 g per teaspoon and Morton kosher salt about 4.8 g. Fine table salt is about 6 g, more than twice as salty by volume as Diamond Crystal.
